text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Hungary and Romania will sign the bilateral basic treaty between the two countries in Timisoara (Romania) on September 16.
- Parliament rejected the opposition's proposal that had treaty only with preliminary authorisation from Parliament.

- Tamas Suchman, candidate for the post of minister of industry and trade, told a parliamentary committee hearing that although a certain adjustment is needed in Hungary's economic policy, failure to attain economic growth in line with expectations does not justify an economic change of direction.
- A Hungarian summit bringing together 10 organisations of Hungarians in the Carpathian Basin and other delegations, but not from the cabinet, held a meeting in Papa behind closed doors.
- The National Bank will close down its 18 county directorates at the end of the year.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. has seen HUF 3.1 billion in revenues from the simplified privatisation programme.
- The Swiss owner of the daily Magyar Hirlap appointed deputy editor-in-chief Ferenc Gazso to the post of editor-in-chief.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Six Free Democrats propose that the Constitutional Court declare null and void those provisions of the secret agents' act which do not guarantee the right of citizens to information.
- Parliament's environmental committee is to begin debating a new bill on nuclear energy shortly.

- Labour market supervisors carried out 9,500 checks affecting 69,000 employees in the first six months of 1996. Supervisors uncovered wrongdoing in 956 cases and initiated criminal proceedings in 53 cases.
-Open-end investment funds are rapidly growing in popularity among Hungarians with capital to invest, the value of their collective assets having almost tripled so far this year.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- The cabinet is expected today to hear a report by the Prime Minister's office on the establishment of a company to run an information science and technological innovation park.
- The $100 million expansion of Terminal 2 at Budapest's Ferihegy Airport may begin within days, said a top government official.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Paper details Hungary's participation at NATO Partnership for Peace exercises.
- The average monthly net wage over the first seven months of 1996 was HUF 30,036, a 19.5 per cent year-on-year rise.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The top executive of Austria's GiroCredit bank, Ferdinand Lacina, arrived in Budapest for talks with Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy and Privatisation Minister Tamas Suchman, presumably concerning his bank's interest in purchasing the trustee savings bank Takarekbank.
NEPSZAVA

- The Hungarian Helsinki Committee, a human rights watchdog, has found no human rights violations in refugee camps at Debrecen and Nagyatad but still finds conditions prevailing in Hungarian police jails to be unsatisfactory.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 266 2410
